title: The Rules of AI Chat History
intro: A chat transcript is a record, not a history.

topics.title: The Rules of AI Chat History

learn.title: Three layers
learn.text:
**1 · Task history** — separate tasks or background jobs the user can reopen, each with a status
**2 · Interaction history** — instructions, clarifications and tool activity: scannable and collapsible
**3 · Output workspace** — reports, drafts and tables, persistent, with the current version obvious

Each layer does a different job. The transcript can stay, but it shouldn't carry the whole experience.

try.q: Which layer holds the finished report the user came for?
try.explain: Persistent, with the current version clearly marked.

learn.title: What counts as a separate task
learn.text:
The most important design decision. A task is **a self-contained request with a goal and a finish point**.

Three questions:

• Is the user still working toward the same outcome?
• Does the new instruction refine the existing output?
• Could earlier context distort the answer?

**A subject change isn't always a new task** — and staying in one thread isn't always right either.

try.q: A user changes subject mid-thread. Is that a new task?
options: Only after a set number of turns
try.explain: The test is whether they're still working toward the same outcome.

learn.title: Why this matters
learn.text:
Without the layers, users scroll through old versions looking for the current one, can't tell whether a background job finished, and lose track of which instruction produced which output.

The transcript is good at one thing: showing what was said. It is bad at status, at versioning and at finding things again.

try.q: What is a transcript genuinely good at?
try.explain: Which is why it's a record rather than a history.

test.q: What does Calabro mean by “a record, not a history”?
options: It logs turns but doesn't organise the work
test.explain: History implies structure the transcript doesn't provide.

test.q: What should task history show besides the task?
test.explain: Including background jobs the user can reopen.

test.q: What should the interaction layer be?
options: Limited to the last ten turns

test.q: When might earlier context be a reason to start a new task?
options: When it could distort the answer
test.explain: One of the three questions for task separation.

test.q: What problem do users hit without an output workspace?
options: Scrolling to find the current version
test.explain: Old versions and the current one look the same in a transcript.
